newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures cling to modest gains late.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures cling to modest gains late.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still up slightly late Wednesday in lackluster trade, but prices remained in recent technical ranges with little reason to move far in either direction, industry sources said.
At 1355 EST, December was still up by 2.9 cents at $2.675 per million British thermal units, while January was 2.7 cents higher at $2.67. Most others were up by one to 2.3 cents.

"I'm not sure but I have bearish leanings. We only got a 10-cent bounce this week from the weather and temperatures next week are due to moderate," said one Houston-based trader, adding it would take sustained cold to retest recent highs.
While most agreed the market lacked conviction and may range trade until clearer weather patterns emerge, few expected the bears to take total control, with an uncertain winter still ahead.
"It's still a 100 percent weather play," said another trader.

Technical traders said the market was range bound, with trendline support in December at $2.59-2.60 and better buying likely at $2.53. Resistance remained at $2.75 and then at the $2.88 contract high.
A Reuter poll of industry players showed most expected U.S. gas inventories to be unchanged to eight bcf higher when AGA releases its weekly gas storage report later today.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices were down slightly to about the $2.70 area. Midwest prices slipped more than a nickel to about $2.60. Cold weather firmed New York city gate swing gas by about 10 cents to the $3.50-60 area.
NYMEX said 17,921 contracts traded at 1320 EST.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas jumped 18 cents to $1.51, while deferreds were untraded. NYMEX Alberta open interest on Nov 12 fell five lots to 432.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded at 1355 EST. NYMEX Permian open interest on Nov 12 was unchanged at 436.
On the KCBT, December was unchanged at $2.465, while deferreds were mixed. The East/West spread widened by 2.9 cents to 21.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
